review_method: Independent visual inspection of retained original regional maps, legends, identified river photograph and river/storage prose with every complete selected baseline path; independent decoding compares exact selected IDs, fragment order, every position and metadata with immutable baseline inputs. Public validation checks included factual linkage only.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs, not individual named rivers or verified reach names.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete eastern basin corresponds at regional scale to water beneath the Lake part of the Sandfly Lake label. Its broad northern cap, western notch, eastern indentation and lower eastward arm taper into the southern tip. The full outline was compared with mapped water and surrounding shore. This supports generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected feature, not equivalence with the entire named lake or extension of that name to connecting river water.

The entire north-south outline corresponds geographically to mapped water between Struga, Ohrid and Pogradec. Its broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long east and west sides and rounded southern end were compared. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from literal wording within a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. Strong shape correspondence does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the complete selected water polygon. No supported whole-water identity or protected-site/water-boundary equivalence is assigned.

findings.follow_up_scope: Obtain legible direct river-name evidence tied to the complete regional corridor before supporting the Richmond River representative identity. Exact upper feeder, river/storage, name-transition and coastal scope also require evidence before separately authorized application.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path runs southeast from a northwestern headwater, south through the upper and middle corridor, then east and northeast after a southern bend to the New South Wales coast south of Lismore. Regional geometry is compatible with the Richmond River candidate, but the clearly legible Richmond River wording in Figure 4.22 is a basin callout. Possible blue river-line lettering in the retained regional maps is too indistinct to certify. Neither basin context nor geographic resemblance establishes a directly named representative river identity here. The whole group remains on a naming-scope hold after complete available-source/path review; the upper feeder, any river/storage interfaces, exact name transitions and coastal ending are unassigned at reach level.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete three-fragment modeled mainstem begins in the southwest, sweeps east around a southern bend, then runs northeast through the upper/storage corridor and curves east toward the coast north of Sydney. The directly identified Hawkesbury River at Little Wobby photograph and the prose identifying Hawkesbury water supply to Richmond-Windsor, together with the full regional path comparison, support Hawkesbury River as a bounded representative system identity. The southwestern upper continuation follows the separately mapped Wollondilly corridor and the Lake Burragorang/Warragamba storage corridor. A modeled mainstem can include differently named feeder reaches. Coxs is a separately named contributor in source prose, not an assignment to a selected branch. Green water-transfer arrows in Figure 4.36 are not natural river geometry. Exact Wollondilly/storage/downstream name transitions, any Nepean or other intermediate naming, river/storage interfaces and the generalized coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: Hawkesbury River basin wording alone is not the identity basis; a named river photograph and river-specific prose provide additional evidence.
Wollondilly and Lake Burragorang/Warragamba remain distinct upper/storage context. Coxs source prose and transfer arrows do not name selected reaches.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path begins in the far north, runs south through the upper storage corridor, turns east, makes a broad westward middle loop, then continues south to the Victorian coast. Direct blue Snowy river-line wording supports Snowy River as a bounded representative system identity. The northern modeled mainstem follows the separately mapped Eucumbene corridor before the downstream Snowy course; a modeled mainstem can include differently named feeder reaches. The mapped lake and Snowy Hydro storage context do not establish exact lake names, river/storage interfaces or name boundaries on the selected line. Exact Eucumbene-to-Snowy transitions, intervening storage/lake scope and the generalized coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.

included_evidence_limit: Only public factual summaries, bibliography and included-file integrity are testable here. Original maps, full selected paths, private decoder inputs and recorded visual judgments cannot be reproduced by public validation. A completed scope review can retain a naming hold; representative identity does not establish every reach name or authorize product use.

inherited_same_name_disambiguation.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path runs southeast from a far-northwestern headwater, turns south through the middle corridor, then bends east and southeast into the Gippsland Lakes coastal complex. Direct blue Mitchell river-line labels support Mitchell River in Victoria as a representative system identity. The long northwestern upper continuation is not individually named by the inspected maps; a modeled mainstem can include differently named feeder reaches and does not make every part Mitchell. Exact feeder-to-river name transitions, any river/storage interfaces and the final generalized line through lake or coastal water remain unassigned at reach level.

The entire selected group includes the northern east-to-west modeled mainstem, its lower northwestward course, the long southern branch and the shorter northern tributary. Direct Mitchell labelling on the lower channel supports Mitchell River as the representative system identity. The upper modeled mainstem follows the regional Palmer corridor and the southern branch follows the Walsh corridor. These are geographic associations, not exact reach-name assignments. The shorter northern tributary, precise transitions and coastal continuation remain individually unnamed.
